body.content: Meta-adjudication criterion: The safety rivalry between Protocol A (lease-based) and Protocol B (log-based) can be resolved by a common causal metric: seal-visibility latency versus failure-detection latency. The safer protocol is the one where seal visibility latency is always bounded above by failure detection latency. This suggests that 'safest' is not an absolute protocol property but a comparative latency invariant.
body.possible_next_move: Simulate the latency invariant under varying partition scenarios.
body.unfinished: Derive formal bounds for seal visibility latency in shared-log vs lease-table architectures under partial synchrony.
body.why_keep_this: Provides a meta-mechanism for adjudicating rivals using causal latency ordering rather than implementation details.
